Khemchanddas on 22 April, 2018

Author: B.N. Karia

IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  LOK ADALAT  R/CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 953 of 2013 ==========================================================
 STATE OF GUJARAT - THRO' K R PATEL, FOOD INSPECTOR  Versus

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Appearance:
MR KL PANDYA, APP for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1 MR KV SHELAT(834) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 5 MR.KIRIT R CHAUDHARI(3745) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1,3,4 RULE NOT RECD BACK(63) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 2 ==========================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE B.N. KARIA  Date : 22/04/2018
ORAL ORDER 1.

This Criminal Appeal preferred under Section 378 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is directed against the judgment and order of acquittal dated 01.09.2012 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Visnagar, in Criminal Case No. 211/1995 acquitting the respondents for an offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
2. This Appeal is taken up for settlement in Lok Adalat.
3. Mr. K.L. Pandya, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has appeared on behalf of the State and has produced withdrawal / settlement pursis, which is taken on record.

The withdrawal / settlement pursis is signed by the authorized signatory, who is R/CR.A/953/2013 ORDER present in person before this Lok Adalat and the pursis is counter signed by learned APP and respective learned advocates.
Original complainant Shri A.B. Ghelani, Food Inspector is not present.

However, on a pursis, Shri C.S. Gohil has put his signature as an authorized person, which is duly identified by Mr.

sentences.text:

1 D.R. Sharma, Law Officer of the Department.
Shri Sharma is present before the Court.
He stated that whatever the order will be passed will be binding to him and he has no objection to the compromise.
The respondent no.3 has expired, and therefore, proceedings qua him stood abated.

However, respondents No. 1 and 4 who are present before this Court have assured of their abiding to the terms of the order that may be passed and they have assured this Court that whatever the fine will be imposed will also be honoured by them.
4.

It is submitted that the offence alleged against the accused under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, is not serious in nature, the penalty / punishment prescribed for such offence is not substantial in view of the Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, it is compoundable under Section 69 of the said Act.
5. In view of the withdrawal / compromise pursis of the parties, this Appeal stands disposed of.

The respondent No. 2 is directed to pay a sum of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand Only) and R/CR.A/953/2013 ORDER respondents No.1, 4 and 5 are directed to pay a sum of Rs. 3,000/-
(Rupees Three thousand only) each (in all, the respondent No. 2 shall pay Rs. 5,000/- and respondents No. 1, 4 and 5 shall together pay Rs. 9,000/-) towards litigation cost, as agreed between the parties, in lieu thereof.
Necessary cost be deposited in the office of the High Court Legal Services Committee within four weeks, failing which the Appeal shall stand revived automatically.
Accordingly, this appeal stands disposed of.

6. However, disposal of this matter will not affect any connected matters arising out of the same,
incidental or any other proceedings, filed or to be filed before any other Court.
It is also required to be noted that this order will not be treated as a precedent in any future case for reference.

(B.N. KARIA, J.) Chairman ksdarji State Of Gujarat - Thro' K R Patel, Food ... vs Patel Ambalalbhai Khemchanddas on 22 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88436189/
